title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) measuring whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The sole guarded improvement arose from a single verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires that generated configurations satisfy deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering/workflow constraints, and safety group constraints). Prior work has prototyped intent→configuration translation and has advocated validation or verification stages, but artifact-grounded evidence quantifying verifier-integrated pipelines under tightly controlled experimental designs is limited [1],[2].

This study asks the preregistered research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? Because the experiment used shared_initial_candidate semantics, the estimand isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect) and does not measure effects of constrained prompting or independent multi-sample strategies.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis based on archived validator traces for the single repaired pair. (5) A bounded interpretation, reproducibility guidance tied to archived artifacts, and explicit threats to validity.
sections.related_work:
Recent NetOps and AIOps literature documents active work on intent-driven configuration synthesis, prototype generator–validator pipelines, and evaluation suites that assess configuration-generation accuracy under curated tasks [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain research on generate→validate→repair (program repair, constrained program synthesis, and LLM-augmented tool chains) motivates guarded pipelines; empirical demonstrations in software engineering often show that verifier-assisted repair can improve correctness under well-scoped oracles [4],[5],[6]. Surveys of agentic AI and LLM safety emphasize common failure modes (hallucination, confabulation) and recommend verifier gates, provenance, and constrained tool access for operational workflows [7],[8].

How our study differs. Unlike prior multi-model benchmark reports that compare aggregate accuracy across independent first-pass generations, our paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics specifically measures the marginal effect of verifier-triggered repair on the identical initial sample. This narrow estimand is useful for quantifying whether a verifier-plus-bounded-repair stage can fix deterministic invariant violations that exist in an initial candidate, but it does not assess alternative mitigation strategies such as constrained prompts, temperature tuning, or multi-sample selection.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, defined as the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). Generation semantics were fixed to shared_initial_candidate in the preregistration; each task produced exactly one initial model generation reused by both baseline and guarded episodes. The protocol permitted at most one automated repair call per task and declared one confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest.

Task bank and deterministic sampling. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and selected deterministically: for zero-based ordinal j in 0..199 the task_index mapping defined in the preregistration was applied (a fixed cycle/offset rule). Tasks targeted very_hard and extreme workflow patterns with multi-device ordering constraints, dependency rules, and group-level invariants. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies; these manifests are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Inclusion/exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks and syntactic pre-checks) were applied before any model calls; no preregistered exclusions occurred in the archived run.

Model configuration, calls, and shared_initial semantics. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini and the file records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly report that temperature = null in the archived model_configuration is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; hosted-model nondeterminism remains possible. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 201 and provider-call audit stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1, hosted_model_call_event_count = 201.

Deterministic verifier and scoring. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the oracle. It applied deterministic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, required_sequence ordering constraints, group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and other dependency rules encoded in the task manifest. The binary outcome used for the primary estimand (full_intent_constraint_validation) is 1 if all required invariants pass and 0 otherwise. The verifier produces per-episode validator traces (validation_before and validation_after) and violation codes; these traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Statistical analysis plan and exact-test details. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar implementation operating on discordant counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). The exact two-sided p-value enumerates the binomial tail for n = n10 + n01 under the null that discordant outcomes are equally likely. For our observed discordants (n = 1 with n10 = 1 and n01 = 0) the two-sided exact McNemar p reported by the analysis executor is 1.0 because the single possible nonzero discordant outcome is not more extreme than its mirror under the two-sided rule. For reproducibility we compute paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the risk difference with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729) as recorded in analysis artifacts.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records start and end timestamps (started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00), planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting. Provider-call audit stage counts are shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). The analysis/condition_summary.csv artifact reports:
- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.
The paired contingency artifact analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv contains the counts: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Statistical inference (artifact numbers). The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar reported p = 1.0 for the observed discordant pattern (n10 = 1, n01 = 0). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]; these parameters and the bootstrap seed are archived in analysis_log.jsonl and analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg. All numbers in this Results section are exact matches to archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and the CSV artifacts referenced above).

Repair activity and representative failure diagnosis. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair (repair stage count = 1). The archived validator_trace for the repaired pair identifies the failure as a multi-step ordering/workflow violation relative to the task's required_sequence. Representative artifacts for the repaired pair are archived (execution/responses/task-000008-*, execution/scoring/task-000008-*). The repair prompt and repaired final configuration are logged in the scoring JSON; after repair the verifier returned valid = true. This single repaired case is the only instance where the guarded path altered verifier acceptance in the archived run.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination monitoring. The execution, analysis, and reconciliation artifacts report no excluded preregistered tasks and no missing pairs: complete_pairs = 200, baseline_only_observed_pairs = 0, guarded_only_observed_pairs = 0, both_missing_pairs = 0. The contamination_summary.csv artifact contains no flagged entries. These artifact records show that the run adhered to the preregistered inclusion/exclusion and contamination-detection rules.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the paired estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because the execution enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics, baseline and guarded conditions started from the identical initial candidate for each task. Therefore the estimand measures the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on that initial sample (a repair-only effect). The study does not measure benefits that would arise from constrained prompting, independent guarded-first-pass prompts, temperature tuning, or multi-sample selection—separate preregistered experiments would be required to estimate those effects.

Statistical power and observed baseline rate. The preregistration targeted detection of ≈10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N = 200 under assumed baseline pass rates ~45–65%. The observed baseline pass rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded those planning assumptions, which substantially reduced realized power for detecting small absolute differences. The discrete nature of discordant counts led to the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the observed single discordant pair; the paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies plausible small absolute improvements consistent with the observed data.

Operational implications and qualified intuition. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach, consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device policy interactions and required_sequence ordering concentrate failure risk. In this synthetic deterministic setting a verifier gate plus a single automated repair sufficed to correct that localized ordering fault. This suggests guarded repair can be effective for sequence-conformance faults where a small, well-formed modification restores invariant compliance. It does not imply effectiveness for other fault classes (e.g., semantic misinterpretation of intent or omissions detectable only through live telemetry).

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and single initial generation per task limit the inferences to repair effects only. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not emulate live dataplane behavior or runtime telemetry; some operational hazards require live-device checks. External validity: results derive from a synthetic, deterministic task bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini); broader generalization requires multi-model and live-device evaluations. Conclusion validity: rare discordant counts imply high sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects; the reported CI and exact-test p-value reflect that discrete regime.

Reproducibility and artifact-grounded verification. All analysis and execution artifacts are archived in the execution bundle. Key artifact identifiers reported here include: execution/model_configuration.json sha256 = "1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa" and the initial master prompt reference path provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = "1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba". The execution manifest reports model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared initial + 1 repair). The analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, analysis_log.jsonl) contain the exact numeric outputs used for inference. Reanalysis is reproducible by running the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl as indexed in execution/execution_manifest.json.

Recommended next steps grounded in the artifacts. To extend operational relevance, future preregistered runs should (1) adopt independent first-pass generation semantics to measure guarded-prompt effects, (2) test multiple models to assess generality beyond gpt-5-mini, (3) expand task diversity and include live-device telemetry checks or emulation, and (4) include adversarial contamination/poisoning experiments. Each recommendation follows directly from limitations observed in the archived run (single model, synthetic tasks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, limited adversarial testing).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with a paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair. The artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived with the execution manifest and hashes in the execution bundle.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
